body_markdown:
Figma AI can generate a polished interface in minutes. The harder question is what happens next. You can turn that mockup into a working web or mobile app using a direct Figma importer or a full-stack app-building platform like[Floot](https://floot.com/) , which works through supported AI assistants. According to Stack Overflow's 2026 survey,[83% of respondents](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2026/ai/data) use at least one AI tool at work, highlighting how widely AI has entered software development workflows.


[AI app builders](https://floot.com/blog/best-ai-app-builders-for-non-technical-founders-in-2026) have closed the gap between design and deployment. Some tools import Figma files directly. Others generate full-stack applications from natural language prompts. Floot, for example, provides managed infrastructure through a[Model Context Protocol](https://floot.com/blog/what-is-mcp-a-simple-guide-to-model-context-protocol-for-ai-apps) (MCP) connector, while your connected AI assistant handles development.


The right choice depends on how you work, what you need to ship, and whether you want to own the code. This guide covers 13 AI app builders for turning Figma AI designs into real, working applications in 2027.


## **Key Takeaways**


- **Build through supported assistants:** Floot is a[full-stack app-building platform](https://floot.com/docs/getting-started/how-floot-works) with an MCP connector for Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations. Available actions depend on client permissions.
- **Use existing AI subscriptions:**[Connector-based building](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) uses your connected assistant rather than separate Floot AI build credits, although platform and hosting charges may apply.
- **Get managed infrastructure:** Floot supplies a[Postgres database](https://floot.com/docs/platform/database) , authentication, file storage, backend services, and hosting for apps that need logins and saved data.
- **Build for web and mobile:** Floot supports[mobile app publishing](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/publishing-to-app-stores) for iOS and Android, with separate developer accounts and store review required.
- **Keep ownership clear:** Floot users own their code and data;[full ZIP export](https://floot.com/docs/faqs/code-data-and-exports) requires a paid plan, and[plan pricing](https://floot.com/en/pricing) includes hosting allowances and usage-based overages.


## **What to Look for in an AI App Builder for Figma Designs**


Turning a Figma design into a working app requires more than generating HTML. Teams evaluating AI app builders should consider how well each tool handles the full workflow from design import to production deployment.


A capable AI app builder for Figma-based workflows should support:


- **Figma integration depth** - Can the tool import Figma files directly, use a plugin, or only accept screenshots? Native import preserves design fidelity better than re-interpretation.
- **Code quality and framework** - What code does the builder generate? React, Next.js, Flutter, and plain HTML serve different purposes. The output should match your team's technical direction.
- **Backend and database support** - Many designs need user authentication, data storage, and server-side logic. Some builders include[managed databases](https://floot.com/docs/platform/database) and backend services, while others require external setup.
- **Mobile app capability** - Not every builder can produce apps for the App Store or Google Play. Some generate responsive web apps, others package native shells, and a few export true mobile code.
- **Code ownership and export** - Can you download your code, sync to GitHub, or self-host? This matters for long-term maintenance and switching platforms.
- **Pricing model** - Some platforms charge per token or generation, others use monthly subscriptions, and a few allow you to use your existing AI assistant without additional model costs.
- **Production readiness** - Hosting, SSL, custom domains, SEO controls, and security features determine whether the output is ready for real users.


## **1. Floot**


Floot is a full-stack app-building platform with an MCP connector that lets users create, edit, and publish applications through supported AI assistants, including Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations. Floot provides managed infrastructure while the connected assistant handles development, with available building capabilities depending on the client's connector permissions. You can[build apps](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) in the AI assistant you already use, or use Floot's optional credit-based AI agent. Floot does not document native Figma file import, so users can describe designs and provide references for the assistant to recreate and refine.


### **Primary Focus**


Floot's approach means you describe your app to a supported AI assistant, which develops it using Floot's managed infrastructure. Connector-based building generally uses the assistant's existing subscription rather than Floot AI build credits, although platform charges and usage-based hosting still apply. The platform provides TypeScript and React projects with managed Postgres, authentication, file storage, and hosting.


### **Key Capabilities**


- Create, edit, and publish apps through supported Claude, Codex, Cursor, and ChatGPT clients, subject to connector permissions
- Use your existing AI subscription for generation
- Managed Postgres database on all plans
- User authentication with Google and Microsoft OAuth
- Web publishing and[mobile app builds](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/creating-mobile-apps-in-floot) for iOS and Android, with separate developer accounts and store review
- SEO controls including[server-side pre-rendering](https://floot.com/en/seo)


### **What Sets Floot Apart**


Floot connects AI assistants to a managed full-stack environment through MCP rather than replacing Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor. The connected assistant handles development within its permitted connector capabilities, while Floot runs the application infrastructure. This supports an iterative workflow in which you describe the design, review the result, and refine it through conversation.


- **Managed data:** A[Postgres database](https://floot.com/docs/platform/database) works on all plans, with browser-based table viewing and export.
- **Authentication and storage:** Email/password sign-in, brokered Google and Microsoft OAuth, and CDN-backed file storage support apps with real users.
- **Mobile delivery:**[Cloud mobile builds](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/publishing-to-app-stores) package web apps for iOS and Android without requiring a Mac or Xcode for Floot-managed builds. Developer accounts and store review are still required.
- **Search visibility:**[SEO controls](https://floot.com/en/seo) include server-side pre-rendering, sitemap management, and page metadata.
- **Practical audience:** For[non-technical founders](https://floot.com/blog/best-ai-app-builders-for-non-technical-founders-in-2026) , Floot handles infrastructure while they build through their preferred assistant.


### **Floot Pricing and Plans**


Floot is[free to start](https://floot.com/en/pricing) . Free includes 100 daily build actions, 2 mobile app builds per month, and a one-time $3 hosting credit. Pro costs $25 per month with 1,000 daily actions, 12 mobile builds per month, custom domains, 5,000 monthly AI credits, and a $10 monthly hosting allowance. Power costs $100 per month with 5,000 daily actions, unlimited mobile builds, 15,000 monthly AI credits, and a $25 hosting allowance. The connected assistant's own subscription is separate from Floot's fees; hosting overages draw on prepaid credit. Connecting Google Play requires a paid Floot plan. Users own their code, data, and intellectual property on every plan, though a full project ZIP download requires a paid Floot plan.


## **2. Figma Make**


Figma Make is an AI app builder integrated directly into the Figma interface. Launched at Config 2025, it lets designers generate functional apps directly from prompts or existing Figma designs without leaving their design environment.


### **Primary Focus**


Figma Make operates inside Figma for teams who already live in Figma and want the shortest path from design to working code. Because it works within Figma, designers avoid context switching between tools. The platform uses actual design system components through Make Kits rather than generating generic UI.


### **Key Capabilities**


- Generate apps from natural language prompts or existing Figma designs
- Use Make Kits to build with design system tokens on eligible plans
- Connect to Supabase for backend functionality
- Push projects to GitHub for version control and handoff
- Integrate with Figma Dev Mode for engineering collaboration


### **Considerations**


Figma Make can be tried on the free Starter plan, although Starter users must also publish to the Figma Community to publish publicly. Professional Full seats start at $16 per month when billed annually, with broader features available on paid plans. The platform supports backend integration through Supabase and one-way GitHub pushes, though teams needing more infrastructure control may want to compare it with full-stack builders.


## **3. Anima**


Anima is a Figma-to-code converter that transforms designs into responsive HTML, React, or Vue code. It reports at least 1.5 million Figma plugin installs and powers Figma workflows inside other major AI builders.


### **Primary Focus**


Anima works for teams that want to export clean, production-ready code from Figma designs. The platform already runs inside Bolt.new and Replit, so if you use those builders, Anima's engine handles the Figma conversion.


### **Key Capabilities**


- Export Figma designs to HTML, React, or Vue code
- Clone full multi-page websites into editable projects
- Match brand styles automatically from any URL
- Import artifacts from Claude or other AI tools
- Use Anima MCP for AI coding agent integration


### **Considerations**


Anima began with design-to-code translation, but Anima Playground now also supports built-in databases and user authentication. Teams with advanced backend requirements should check whether its capabilities fit their needs.


## **4. Lovable**


Lovable is a full-stack AI builder that generates complete applications from natural language descriptions. In November 2026, the company reported 70 million user-created projects and more than 1 billion monthly visits to Lovable-built applications.


### **Primary Focus**


Lovable handles the entire stack, including frontend, backend, database, authentication, and hosting. Enterprise customers like Adidas, Asana, and Nvidia use the platform for rapid prototyping and internal tools.


### **Key Capabilities**


- Build full-stack applications from text prompts
- Use Lovable Cloud's managed backend or connect a separate Supabase project for authentication and data storage
- Accept payments in over 200 countries through Stripe integration
- Sync code to GitHub for ownership and version control
- Deploy with built-in hosting and SSL


### **Considerations**


Lovable is free to start, with paid plans at $25 per month for Pro and $50 per month for Business. The platform imports Figma designs, though the workflow centers on prompt-based generation rather than Figma-native integration. For a Floot-specific view, see the[builder comparison](https://floot.com/blog/floot-vs-lovable-compare-ai-no-code-platforms-2025) .


## **5. Builder.io Fusion**


Builder.io Fusion generates production-ready code that connects to your existing codebase and design system. It understands your components, tokens, and patterns rather than creating generic output.


### **Primary Focus**


Fusion is designed for teams that want AI-generated code to fit their existing architecture. The platform imports Figma designs through a plugin and generates code using your actual React components and design tokens.


### **Key Capabilities**


- Import Figma designs and transform them to production code
- Generate code using your existing components and design system
- Connect to your repository's APIs and business logic
- Capture design inspiration from any website via Chrome extension
- Generate React code using connected components and design systems


### **Considerations**


Builder.io Fusion targets teams with established codebases who want AI assistance that respects their architecture. The platform is more developer-oriented than purely no-code builders and assumes some technical context.


## **6. Bolt.new**


Bolt.new is an AI coding agent from the StackBlitz team that generates full-stack applications with automatic model routing. The platform is trusted by Google, Microsoft, Salesforce, and other enterprise customers.


### **Primary Focus**


Bolt.new emphasizes code quality through automatic testing, refactoring, and context management designed to support larger projects. Its browser-based development environment combines AI code generation with services for running and deploying the resulting application.


### **Key Capabilities**


- Automatic model routing selects the right AI for each task
- Bolt Cloud provides databases, authentication, hosting, and analytics
- Design system integration builds with your brand assets
- Partner with Anima for Figma-to-code workflows
- GitHub sync for code ownership


### **Considerations**


Bolt.new uses usage-based pricing with a free tier available. Teams wanting Figma integration work through the Anima partnership rather than native Figma import. The platform is well-suited for teams prioritizing code quality and testing. Floot also offers a[Bolt comparison](https://floot.com/blog/floot-vs-bolt-which-ai-app-builder-is-better-in-2026) .


## **7. Replit Agent**


Replit Agent is an AI development environment that builds applications, websites, presentations, and more. The platform recently launched Agent 4 with multi-user collaboration and intelligent cost management.


### **Primary Focus**


Replit goes beyond app building to support websites, slides, 3D games, and documents. The platform includes an Infinite Canvas for visual design exploration and free mode for brainstorming without token costs.


### **Key Capabilities**


- Build apps, websites, presentations, and other formats
- Free mode allows brainstorming without usage charges
- Replit reported that internal testing produced the same output quality at 65% lower cost than the previous version of Max Mode
- Full-stack infrastructure with authentication, database, and hosting
- Enterprise integrations with Databricks and Lakebase


### **Considerations**


Replit offers a free tier with paid plans at $20 per month for Core and $100 per month for Pro. The platform supports Figma import but operates primarily as a development environment rather than a Figma-native tool.


## **8. v0 by Vercel**


v0 is Vercel's AI UI generator that creates React and Next.js code from prompts. The platform has evolved to support full-stack projects with databases and APIs.


### **Primary Focus**


v0 integrates tightly with the Vercel ecosystem, making it a natural fit for teams already using Next.js. The platform pushes directly to GitHub and deploys through Vercel hosting.


### **Key Capabilities**


- Generate React and Next.js code from natural language
- Create full-stack projects with database and API support
- Push directly to GitHub with pull request workflows
- Deploy through Vercel hosting infrastructure
- Automated security checks during code generation and before deployment


### **Considerations**


v0 uses usage-based pricing with a free tier. The platform serves developers comfortable with the React and Vercel ecosystem. Teams wanting visual or no-code approaches may find other builders more accessible.


## **9. Bubble**


Bubble is an established visual app builder that added AI generation capabilities to its mature platform. The service has operated since 2012 and holds SOC 2 Type II compliance.


### **Primary Focus**


Bubble offers a mature visual logic engine in the no-code space. The platform handles complex workflows, database relationships, and business logic through its visual editor, allowing users to refine application behavior without directly editing the underlying source code.


### **Key Capabilities**


- Visual interface builder with AI-assisted generation
- Powerful workflow and logic engine
- Native iOS and Android apps on paid plans
- SOC 2 Type II compliant infrastructure
- MCP integration in beta for AI agents to work with Bubble apps


### **Considerations**


Bubble pricing starts at $32 per month for web apps when billed annually, with higher tiers for native mobile apps. The platform is web-first rather than Figma-native, and mobile app publishing requires paid plans.


## **10. FlutterFlow**


FlutterFlow is a visual Flutter builder that outputs cross-platform code for iOS, Android, and web. The platform allows code export on paid plans for true ownership.


### **Primary Focus**


FlutterFlow generates Flutter code, which provides true cross-platform capability from a single codebase. Teams can download the Flutter project and continue development independently.


### **Key Capabilities**


- Visual development with Flutter code output
- Cross-platform support for iOS, Android, and web
- Firebase and Supabase backend integration
- Code export for independent development
- Component marketplace for faster building


### **Considerations**


FlutterFlow's Basic plan costs $39 per month on monthly billing, with a lower annual rate. Code download is included on Basic and higher plans. The platform uses Flutter rather than React, which influences the development path and team skill requirements. Figma frame import is available on the Business tier.


## **11. Base44**


Base44 is a conversational AI builder with comprehensive infrastructure including backend, storage, payments, and analytics. The platform offers a Canvas view for visual collaboration.


### **Primary Focus**


Base44 combines vibe coding with built-in infrastructure so teams can describe what they want and get a complete application. The platform includes Superagents for automating workflows within applications.


### **Key Capabilities**


- Vibe coding through natural language descriptions
- Backend, storage, integrations, and payments included
- Superagents automate workflows and processes
- Canvas view for visual page organization
- SEO dashboard with AI-powered recommendations


### **Considerations**


Base44 offers a free tier with paid plans starting at $16 per month when billed annually. The platform does not have native Figma import, so teams would describe their designs through prompts rather than importing files directly. The[Floot alternatives guide](https://floot.com/blog/best-lovable-alternatives-in-2026-apps-that-can-actually-ship) offers additional context on full-stack workflows.


## **12. GlideOS**


GlideOS builds business applications from spreadsheets, prompts, or files. The platform focuses on connected internal tools, workflows, and business dashboards.


### **Primary Focus**


GlideOS uses spreadsheet data as a starting point for building connected business apps. Teams should distinguish GlideOS from the older Glide Classic product when comparing features and pricing.


### **Key Capabilities**


- Build business apps from spreadsheet files or natural-language prompts
- Mobile-first responsive layouts
- Role-based access controls
- Private apps for internal company use


### **Considerations**


GlideOS Basic starts at $25 per month, while Plus starts at $50 per month and includes public app publishing. The platform focuses on browser-based business applications rather than native App Store or Google Play publishing. It is particularly suited to internal tools and data-driven dashboards.


## **13. ChatGPT Sites**


ChatGPT Sites lets users create, preview, publish, and share interactive websites and lightweight web apps directly inside ChatGPT.


### **Primary Focus**


ChatGPT Sites works for teams that want to turn conversations, documents, and data into shareable web experiences without moving to a separate development environment.


### **Key Capabilities**


- Generate interactive websites and lightweight apps from prompts
- Publish and share sites with configurable access controls
- Build data-backed experiences with persistent storage
- Connect supported apps using visitors' existing permissions
- Refine and redeploy websites through ChatGPT


### **Considerations**


ChatGPT Sites is available on eligible paid ChatGPT plans, with building and editing counting toward Codex usage. It is not a documented direct Figma-to-code importer, so matching a Figma design may require additional prompting and refinement. Teams needing native mobile app publishing or a specific managed full-stack infrastructure setup should compare its capabilities with platforms like Floot.


## **Why Floot Delivers Complete Infrastructure for AI-Built Apps**


Floot is a full-stack app-building platform with an MCP connector that works alongside supported AI assistants, including Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations. Your connected assistant handles development within its available permissions, while Floot manages the app's infrastructure. The[connector guide](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) explains this workflow.

- **Publishing:** Hosting, custom domains, and[SEO tools](https://floot.com/en/seo) support web launches; mobile workflows support iOS and Android, subject to store requirements.

Floot is[free to start](https://floot.com/en/pricing) , with paid plans for higher daily building limits and hosting allowances. Connector-based development uses your existing AI subscription rather than a second Floot AI build-credit charge. This setup suits founders and operators who want working applications without configuring infrastructure themselves.


## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **Can AI app builders convert complex Figma designs into functional apps?**


Yes, though accuracy varies by tool. Figma Make and Anima work directly with Figma files, which can help preserve design details. Prompt-based builders like Lovable and Floot generate interfaces from descriptions, which may require refinement to match a specific design exactly. Builder.io Fusion connects to your existing design system to maintain consistency. Floot does not document native Figma import, so use design references and clear instructions with your connected assistant.


### **What backend support should I expect from AI app builders?**


Full-stack builders like Floot, Lovable, Bolt.new, and Replit include managed databases, authentication, and server-side logic. Figma-native tools like Figma Make connect to external backends like Supabase. Anima's design-to-code tools focus on frontend output, but Anima Playground also supports built-in databases and authentication. Floot's[managed database](https://floot.com/docs/platform/database) supports persistent application data without separate infrastructure setup.


### **How do AI app builders handle mobile app publishing?**


Publishing to the App Store and Google Play requires separate developer accounts regardless of which builder you use. Apple charges $99 per year for the Developer Program, and Google Play has a one-time $25 registration fee. Floot, Bubble, and FlutterFlow support mobile builds, but store approval is not guaranteed. Floot's[mobile publishing guide](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/publishing-to-app-stores) explains its managed build and store-submission workflow.


### **Is coding knowledge necessary when using AI app builders?**


Most AI app builders work without coding knowledge for standard applications. Floot, Lovable, and Base44 use natural language for the build process. FlutterFlow and Bubble provide visual editors. However, complex customizations, API integrations, or specific business logic may benefit from technical understanding even on no-code platforms. For Floot, the connected assistant's available building actions also depend on its MCP connector permissions.


### **How does Floot's connector affect app ownership and code export?**


Floot works alongside Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations through MCP. The assistant handles development while Floot provides hosting, Postgres, authentication, and other managed services. Users own their code, data, and intellectual property on every plan. A runnable ZIP export requires a paid Floot plan and must be downloaded through the browser. See Floot's[code export guide](https://floot.com/docs/faqs/code-data-and-exports) for the exact process.
